newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius rupee weakens on dollar and pound.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius rupee weakens on dollar and pound.

text.p: The Mauritian rupee weakened against both the dollar and pound on Wednesday, dealers said.
The rupee was fixed at a mean commercial rate of 20.6720 against the dollar from 20.6275 on Tuesday. The rupee weakened to a mean rate of 32.8070 for one pound from 32.6175 on Tuesday.
Dealers said despite central bank intervention on Tuesday, the rupee was fixed weaker on the dollar mainly to reflect the strong American currency in overnight international markets.
The central bank intervened in the interbank forex market on Tuesday by selling dollars at the prevailing interbank rate, dealers said.
"Several banks were demanding dollars yesterday and some relief has been brought by the central bank's intervention. Banks are still slightly short now," one dealer said.
The dealer said demand for foreign exchange at the time being was principally from importers for their regular payments.
Forex demand was also seen as being subdued for this period of year as compared to the previous years, reflecting a decline of activities in the local commercial sector.
"This is the time when importers usually buy for the end of year festivities. But it looks that they are not very active this time," the dealer said.
